sentence_stem: Not only did the train arrive late,
correct_completion: but the station was also closed for repairs.
full_sentence: Not only did the train arrive late, but the station was also closed for repairs.
acceptable_variants: but the platform was also flooded.
but the ticket office was also closed.

options.text: so we took a taxi instead.
options.why_wrong: This expresses a result of the delay, but 'not only ... but also' needs a second problem added in parallel, not a consequence.

options.text: but the station was also closed for repairs.
and we had to wait outside.
options.why_wrong: This describes what happened next, but it does not complete the 'not only ... but also' pattern with a parallel second problem.
'Although' introduces a contrast with the first clause, but the structure requires 'but also' to add a second parallel point.

grammar_focus: Negative inversion with 'not only ... but also'
explanation: After 'Not only', the auxiliary verb 'did' is placed before the subject, which is the inversion. The second clause must start with 'but also' to add a parallel problem of the same kind. Polish speakers often keep normal word order after 'not only', so the inversion is easy to forget.
translation: Nie tylko pociąg przyjechał spóźniony, ale także stacja była zamknięta z powodu remontu.
